steps.title: Single-warp 16×8 tile: load fragments directly from global
XOR swizzle: ldmatrix without bank conflicts

cases.name: one_atom
cases.purpose: Exactly one mma: if any A/B/C fragment coordinate is wrong, the result is not exactly equal.

cases.name: atoms
cases.purpose: Several 16×8 tiles, several K slices: checks the warp/block-to-tile mapping and the accumulation over the K loop.

cases.name: long_k
cases.purpose: Very long K, random values: the accumulators stay in registers for the whole K loop, and the error should grow with sqrt(K).

cases.name: aligned
cases.purpose: Exact multiples of the CTA tile, 3 tiles along N: checks the position of each warp in the CTA and the ldmatrix addresses, with exact comparison.

cases.name: tiny
cases.purpose: Smaller than one mma, K only 8: out-of-bounds rows, columns and K must be zero-filled instead of read out of bounds.

cases.name: tail
cases.purpose: M and N both odd and not tile multiples, K = 32 + 8: checks the zero fill and the write-back bounds checks of the tail tiles.

cases.name: random
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, K not a multiple of 32.

cases.name: square
cases.purpose: Tensor Core throughput: 137 GFLOP, 64 MB of input.

cases.name: wide
cases.purpose: Larger M, N: C is 256 MB, larger than L2; checks how the tile schedule behaves on a large grid.
